answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond before it can earn trust-weighted work. After a task, randomly selected counterparties attest to delivery; proven fraud slashes the bond and reduces future access, while honest work gradually builds a history. A velvet interface, quill-signed receipts, and a karst-like ledger of linked claims may aid review, but the deterrent is the stake: an attacker must lock real capital into every Sybil and risk losing it.
